salesforce.their_pitch: Enterprise market leader with the biggest ecosystem and brand recognition.
salesforce.weakness: Sticker price excludes mandatory implementation partners; typical mid-market deployment runs 6+ months and total cost of ownership is 2.4x license cost (Forrester TEI).
proof_points: Average Salesforce implementation takes 6-9 months vs weeks on our platform
Einstein AI features are gated behind the $165/user Unlimited tier
G2 reports 41% of switchers cite 'unexpected admin overhead' as the top pain
salesforce.pricing_angle: Per-seat license plus admin headcount; our flat plan is typically 38% cheaper at their scale.
salesforce.rebuttal: I totally understand the Salesforce appeal -- everyone evaluates them. What most teams discover is that the license is only about 40% of the real cost once you add the implementation partner and a dedicated admin. For a team your size that's usually a 2.4x multiplier and a six-month rollout before you see value. You're live on our platform today and your workflows are already built -- switching resets that clock.

hubspot.their_pitch: Friendly all-in-one suite with a generous free tier and strong marketing tools.
hubspot.weakness: The free tier is a funnel into per-seat and per-contact pricing that scales aggressively; enterprise features require the Professional/Enterprise tiers where costs triple.
proof_points: Contact-tier pricing grows with the database, not with usage
Enterprise-grade reporting requires the $800+/mo Professional tier
Native automation depth is capped -- complex workflows force paid Operations Hub add-ons
hubspot.pricing_angle: Looks cheaper at signup; at their contact volume the real bill typically lands 55-70% higher than ours within a year.
hubspot.rebuttal: HubSpot's free tier is genuinely nice -- the catch is that it's priced per contact and per seat, so the bill compounds as you grow. Teams at your scale typically see the real cost land 60% higher than ours within the first year, and the reporting you'd need lives in their Enterprise tier. I'd rather show you the actual three-year cost curve than let you find out mid-contract.

linear.their_pitch: Fast, opinionated issue tracker loved by engineering teams.
linear.weakness: Excellent for eng-led issue tracking but not a revenue platform -- no CRM, no billing, no customer-facing workflows, so it replaces only a slice of the stack.
proof_points: Covers issue tracking only -- you still need CRM, billing, and reporting elsewhere
No built-in revenue or account hierarchy views for GTM teams
Data export is JSON-only; migration back is manual
linear.pricing_angle: Cheap per seat but adds a second vendor; consolidating on us removes an integration and a bill.
linear.rebuttal: Linear is a great tool for pure engineering issue tracking -- I'd never argue otherwise. But it only covers one slice of what you run on us: issues, yes, but not CRM, billing, or your customer workflows. Moving eng to Linear means paying us AND them, plus maintaining a sync between the two. Consolidation is usually the bigger win.

acme.their_pitch: Low-cost challenger promising feature parity at half the price.
acme.weakness: Thin support bench (no named CSM, 48h SLA) and an immature enterprise feature set -- SSO/SAML and audit logging only shipped last quarter.
proof_points: No named customer success manager; best-effort support with a 48h SLA
SSO/SAML and audit logs shipped recently and lack SOC 2 Type II coverage
No migration tooling -- customers rebuild integrations by hand
acme.pricing_angle: Headline price is lower, but missing compliance features force paid workarounds; we beat them on risk-adjusted cost.
acme.rebuttal: I've seen Acme's pricing -- on the sticker it looks like half of ours. The part that doesn't make the slide is that their enterprise features are brand new: SSO and audit logging shipped last quarter and aren't covered by their SOC 2 report yet. For a company with your compliance needs that's real risk. And their support is a 48-hour best-effort queue -- you have a named team with us today.

_generic.their_pitch: A competing platform promising a better deal.
_generic.weakness: Switching costs are real: data migration, re-integration, and team retraining typically consume a full quarter of productivity.
proof_points: Migration projects average 90 days for accounts at your scale
Every integration and workflow would need to be rebuilt and re-tested
Your team's existing playbooks and reporting history don't transfer
_generic.pricing_angle: Any headline discount rarely survives the migration cost and the first renewal.
_generic.rebuttal: Completely fair to look at alternatives -- smart teams do. What I'd flag is the switching cost: migration, re-integration, and retraining usually eat a full quarter of productivity, and your reporting history doesn't transfer. Before you absorb that, let me make staying worth your while.
